findings.message: `read_upload` joins a client-supplied name onto `UPLOAD_DIR` without validation. A name like `../../etc/passwd` or an absolute path such as `/etc/passwd` escapes the upload directory, so any readable file on the server can be fetched.
The `download` handler never checks who is asking or whether the requested file belongs to them. Any caller can read every other user's uploads just by guessing names.

Calling `.decode()` on the file bytes raises `UnicodeDecodeError` for binary uploads such as images or PDFs. A missing file or an empty `file` parameter (which resolves to the directory itself) raises `FileNotFoundError` or `IsADirectoryError`. In all of these cases the client gets a 500 instead of the file or a 404.
This adds a new download endpoint, a change in behaviour, but no test comes with it.
